newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ten detained in France after anti-far right march.
newsitem.headline: Ten detained in France after anti-far right march.

text.p: Police said they detained 10 people after marchers in an anti-far right protest broke shop windows and smashed equipment in regional government offices in Lille, northern France on Wednesday.
The march had been timed to coincide with a campaign rally in Lille by French extreme-right leader Jean-Marie Le Pen and his National Front party.

Critics accuse the Front of being racist and anti-semitic, but opinion polls predict it will draw 14 to 15 percent of the vote and win a seat or two in the National Assembly in a snap May 25-June 1 parliamentary election.
The anti-far right demonstration drew an estimated 4,000 to 5,000 protesters.

Le Pen told supporters he hoped to win more than 20 percent of the vote in the election, which he said conservative President Jacques Chirac had called in order to obtain "a blank check...for a federal Europe".
